review.translation: [Then she again|0] [gave birth to|1] [his brother|2,3] [Abel|4,5]. [Now|6] [Abel|7] [was|6] [a keeper of|8] [flocks|9], [and Cain|10] [was|11] [a tiller of|12] [the soil|13].

analysis.evidence: The infinitive לָלֶדֶת supplies the repeated action. After giving birth to Cain, Eve gives birth again, this time to his brother Abel.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil wayyiqtol, third-person feminine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.evidence: לָלֶדֶת follows וַתֹּסֶף, expressing what Eve did again. The direct object אֶת־אָחִיו אֶת־הָבֶל identifies the child she bore as Cain’s brother Abel.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with prefixed לָ־

analysis.evidence: The marked אֶת introduces אָחִיו (“his brother”) as the direct object of לָלֶדֶת (“to give birth to”). The possessive suffix makes אָחִיו definite. The following אֶת הָבֶל identifies the brother as Abel.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without a prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַתֹּסֶף לָלֶדֶת אֶת־אָחִיו אֶת־הָבֶל, the mother gives birth again. אֶת־הָבֶל names the child described as אָחִיו. The suffix refers to Cain, whose brother Abel is.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: In לָלֶדֶת אֶת אָחִיו אֶת הָבֶל, the marked second אֶת introduces the name הָבֶל in apposition to אָחִיו. Together they identify the direct object of לָלֶדֶת, “his brother Abel.”
analysis.morphology: Direct-object particle without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The repeated direct-object marker in אֶת־אָחִיו אֶת־הָבֶל identifies Abel by name as the brother she bore. The next clause repeats the name in its ordinary form, הֶבֶל.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular personal name in pausal form, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי links הֶבֶל to רֹעֵה צֹאן, “a keeper of sheep.” The parallel clause וְקַיִן הָיָה עֹבֵד אֲדָמָה likewise describes Cain by his occupation.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed conjunction וַ־. The verb agrees with הֶבֶל and has no suffix.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: The birth clause names Cain’s brother הָבֶל. The marked הֶבֶל resumes that name as the subject of וַיְהִי הֶבֶל רֹעֵה צֹאן, identifying Abel as a shepherd. The parallel clause names Cain and gives his occupation.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun in the absolute state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In רֹעֵה צֹאן, the construct participle identifies Abel by the animals he tends. The parallel עֹבֵד אֲדָמָה identifies Cain by the ground he cultivates.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular construct, without prefix or suffix

analysis.evidence: In רֹעֵה צֹאן, “one who tends a flock,” צֹאן names the animals Abel tends. The parallel עֹבֵד אֲדָמָה, “one who works the soil,” identifies Cain’s occupation.
analysis.morphology: Common noun of common gender, singular absolute, collective in meaning, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: the flock in a shepherd's care

draft.definition: Cain, the son of Adam and Eve and brother of Abel.
draft.evidence: Genesis 4:1 names Eve’s son קַיִן. Genesis 4:2 identifies Abel as his brother and names Cain again when describing his work.

analysis.evidence: The verse calls Abel אָחִיו, “his brother,” then describes each brother’s work. וְקַיִן introduces the second subject: Abel tended sheep, and Cain worked the ground.
analysis.morphology: Conjunction וְ prefixed to a masculine singular personal name. קַיִן is the subject of הָיָה.
analysis.sense: The personal name of Abel’s brother.

analysis.evidence: הָיָה agrees with קַיִן and links him to עֹבֵד אֲדָמָה, “a tiller of the soil.” The parallel description of Abel as רֹעֵה צֹאן, “a keeper of sheep,” shows that the verse describes each brother’s occupation.
analysis.morphology: Qal perfect, third person masculine singular, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.evidence: עֹבֵד takes אֲדָמָה (“soil”) as its complement. The phrase עֹבֵד אֲדָמָה names Cain’s occupation, parallel to רֹעֵה צֹאן (“keeper of sheep”) for Abel.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular construct

analysis.evidence: עֹבֵד אֲדָמָה describes Cain as one who works the soil, alongside Abel, who tends a flock (רֹעֵה צֹאן).
analysis.morphology: Common noun, feminine singular absolute, without prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: the ground that is tilled; soil
